cues.zh: （空灵的背景音乐：咿——哦——）
cues.en: (Ethereal background music: Meeeeee, ohhhhhhh)

cues.zh: 1996年，天文学家
cues.en: Astronomers in 1996

cues.zh: 试图做一件非同寻常的事。
cues.en: attempted to do something extraordinary.

cues.zh: 他们把哈勃太空望远镜对准一片看起来空无一物的天空：那里没有行星、
cues.en: They pointed the Hubble Space Telescope into a part of the sky that seemed utterly empty; a patch devoid of any planets,

cues.zh: 恒星和星系。
cues.en: stars and galaxies.

cues.zh: 这片区域靠近北斗七星，这个星座大家都很熟悉。那片天空的大小还不及伸直手臂时
cues.en: This area was close to the Big Dipper, a very familiar constellation, and the patch of sky was no bigger than a grain of sand

cues.zh: 手里捏着的一粒沙子。
cues.en: held out at arm's length.

cues.zh: 科学家们此举多少有些冒险。
cues.en: This was a somewhat risky move by the scientists.

cues.zh: 毕竟，这台望远镜的观测时间十分抢手，有人质疑，把时间花在观测一片虚无上是不是白费功夫。
cues.en: After all, observing time on this telescope is in very high demand and some questioned whether it would be wasted trying to look at nothing

cues.zh: 返回的图像确实有可能和望远镜所指向的太空一样漆黑。
cues.en: There was a real risk that the images returned would be as black as the space at which it was being pointed.

cues.zh: 尽管如此，他们还是启动了望远镜，在整整十天里慢慢地
cues.en: Nevertheless, they opened the telescope and slowly over the course of ten full days,

cues.zh: 那些飞行了130多亿年的光子，终于在
cues.en: photons that had been traveling for over 13 billion years finally ended their journey on the detector of

cues.zh: 人类最强大的望远镜的探测器上结束了旅程。微弱的信号被收集起来，
cues.en: humanity's most powerful telescope. Their feeble signals collected

cues.zh: 几乎是一个一个地。
cues.en: almost one by one.

cues.zh: 当望远镜最终关闭，图像处理完毕后，来自超过
cues.en: When the telescope was finally closed, and the images were processed, the light from over

cues.zh: 3000个星系的光已经覆盖了探测器
cues.en: 3,000 galaxies had covered the detector

cues.zh: 产生了人类历史上最深刻、最令人谦卑的图像之一。
cues.en: producing one of the most profound and humbling images in all of human history.

cues.zh: 每一个斑点、条纹和圆点都是一个完整的星系，每个星系包含数千亿颗恒星。
cues.en: Every single spot, smear, and dot was an entire galaxy, and each one containing hundreds of billions of stars.

cues.zh: 2004年晚些时候，他们又做了一次。这次将望远镜对准猎户座附近的一个区域。
cues.en: Later in 2004, they did it again. This time pointing the telescope towards an area near the constellation Orion.

cues.zh: 他们打开快门超过11天，完成了400次完整的绕地球轨道运行。
cues.en: They opened the shutter for over 11 days and 400 complete orbits around the Earth.

cues.zh: 使用灵敏度更高的探测器和允许更多光线通过的滤镜
cues.en: Using detectors with increased sensitivity and filters that allowed more light through than ever before

cues.zh: 超过一万个星系出现在后来被称为“超深空场”的图像中，
cues.en: over ten thousand galaxies appeared in what became known as the Ultra Deep Field,

cues.zh: 这张图像代表了我们有史以来观测到的最远的宇宙深处。
cues.en: an image that represented the farthest we've ever seen into the universe.

cues.zh: 这些星系发出的光子在宇宙诞生仅 5 亿年时启程，
cues.en: The photons from these galaxies left when the universe was only 500 million years old, and

cues.zh: 在 130 亿年后，化作望远镜 CCD 上的一个微弱光点，结束了漫长的旅途。
cues.en: 13 billion years later they end their long journey as a small blip on a telescope CCD.

cues.zh: 这些星系本身完全静止，却在飞速远离我们，有时甚至超过了光速。
cues.en: These galaxies while standing absolutely still are racing away from us, in some cases, faster than the speed of light.

cues.zh: 我们与万物之间的时空每分每秒都在膨胀，把图像中的星系推到了 470 亿
cues.en: The space-time between us and everything else grows larger by the minute, pushing the galaxies in this image to a distance of over 47 billion

cues.zh: 光年之外。
cues.en: light years.

cues.zh: 由于宇宙膨胀，一个物体离我们越远，它的光红移就越严重，看起来
cues.en: And because of universal expansion the farther something is away from us the more its light has shifted toward the red and the faster it appears

cues.zh: 移动得也就越快。
cues.en: to be moving.

cues.zh: Edwin Hubble 本人通过测量众多星系的红移发现了这一点，这不仅能衡量速度，也能衡量距离。
cues.en: Edwin Hubble himself discovered this by measuring the red shift of many galaxies, and it's a measure of not only speed, but distance as well.

cues.zh: （空灵的背景音乐：啊，啊，啊，啊……啊，啊……）
cues.en: (Ethereal background music: Ah, ah, ah, ahhhh, ah, ah...)

cues.zh: 最近，哈勃望远镜的科学家们又锦上添花。
cues.en: Recently, Hubble scientists put the icing on the cake.

cues.zh: 利用测得的图像中所有星系的红移，他们构建了超深空场的 3D 模型。
cues.en: Using the measured red shifts of all the galaxies inside the image, they made a 3-D model of the Ultra Deep Field.

cues.zh: 将星系间的距离应用到这张史上最重要的图像上后，它看起来就是这样的。
cues.en: This is how it looks when we apply the distances of the galaxies in the most important image ever taken.

cues.zh: 宇宙中有超过 1000 亿个星系。
cues.en: There are over 100 billion galaxies in the universe.

cues.zh: 仅仅说出这个数字对我们而言并没有太大意义，因为它脱离了具体的背景参照。
cues.en: Simply saying that number doesn't really mean much to us because it doesn't provide any context.

cues.zh: 我们的大脑根本无法将其准确代入到任何有意义的认知维度中。
cues.en: Our brains have no way to accurately put that in any meaningful perspective.

cues.zh: 然而，当我们注视着这张图像，思考它是如何拍摄出来的背景，并真正理解其意义时，
cues.en: When we look at this image, however, and think about the context of how it was made and really understand what it means,

cues.zh: 我们瞬间就拥有了那种宏大的视角，并且情不自禁地被它彻底改变。
cues.en: we instantly gain the perspective and cannot help, but be forever changed by it.

cues.zh: 我们把人类有史以来建造的最强大的望远镜对准了空无一物的地方
cues.en: We pointed the most powerful telescope ever built by human beings at absolutely nothing

cues.zh: 纯粹是因为好奇，而且
cues.en: for no other reason than because we were curious, and

cues.zh: 发现我们在天空中占据的位置极其微小。
cues.en: discovered that we occupy a very tiny place in the heavens.
